Changes affect every session in that profile and survive restart. The row id and its reason are in the shipped patch, `packages/bundle/*/cordis.patch.yml` in a source checkout. Write a workspace bundle whose patch overrides that row with `disabled: false` and inserts the Host rows it depends on; a source checkout's `apps/cli/config/examples/<feature>/cordis.yml` lists them for opt-in features. Packages shipped with dsh resolve from the dsh installation, so the bundle declares no dependencies on them. Install it with `install_bundle`.\n\n## Deliver a working plugin first\n\n1. Resolve the requested result and destination. An unspecified visual destination is the current Harness Web UI; a standalone image or HTML file does not complete such a request. Choose reasonable visual details and implement a small first version; install it before visual refinement.\n2. Read the matching template under `templates/` with the file-read tool and write its copies into one workspace directory, or write the installable package, patch, and required Host/Client files there yourself. Use the installed plugin itself as the first preview.\n4. Read the installation result: its `application` and `warnings` fields decide whether the change is live, not server logs, terminal output, process lists, or the page's boot payload. Confirm new rows with `cordis_inspect_query`, which needs no approval, rather than paging `list_plugins`. After `application: applied`, exercise the capability or inspect the live Client registration. Use the connected page for visual verification when browser control is available. For a page or panel, also verify design consistency: styles use only theme tokens, the plugin imports no Harness Client package such as `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives`, the console shows no slot entry crash, and the view reads correctly in light and dark themes beside a comparable host page. Inspection: `cordis_inspect_query` answers exact Service methods and Event modes (`Service`, `Event`), a mounted plugin's Config JSON Schema (`Config.listConfigs`: filter the paged directory by `name`, then query the `entry` id), the Tools this Agent can call (`Tool`), and live Client Slots and theme tokens (`Slots`, `Theme`).\n2. Package documentation: `Config.listConfigs` with `name` set to the package finds its entries; querying one `entry` returns its `packageDir`, the resolved package directory. Read `<packageDir>/README.md`. Bundled packages resolve from the dsh installation and profile-installed bundles from the profile, so never guess the path from `$DSH_PROFILE_DIR`.\n3. Source: installed packages ship built `lib/index.js` and `lib/types/**/*.d.ts` with JSDoc under that same `packageDir`, not `src/`; a source checkout of DSH has `packages/<group>/<name>/src`. Read them when inspection and the README leave a question open, and start source-level diagnosis from a concrete installation or runtime failure.\n\n`DSH_PROFILE` (profile name) and `DSH_PROFILE_DIR` (its directory, whose `node_modules` holds only profile-installed bundles) are set in every shell call of a profile-launched Harness and absent when the Harness was booted without a profile. Bash reads them as `$DSH_PROFILE`; PowerShell, which the Windows preset uses, reads them as `$env:DSH_PROFILE`. With `dsh` on the PATH, `dsh --profile \"$DSH_PROFILE\" --dump-config` prints the composed profile.\n\n## Read next\n\nThe files below live in this skill's base directory, which the `skill` tool reported, and the table is the complete list: do not enumerate that directory. #28 tool/result tool-result "<path>C:\\projects\\dsh_plugins\\dsh-context-sniper\\lib\\index.js</path>\n<type>file</type>\n<content>\n1: // dsh-context-sniper — host half.\n2: //\n3: // A lossless context-saver for long DSH conversations. If it frees context it returns a\n81:   // terminal `{ kind: \"retry\" }` (compaction never runs); otherwise it calls\n82:   // next() and lets the lossy summarizer handle the remainder.\n83:   // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n84:   const TIMEOUT_CODES = new Set(['TIMEOUT', 'ABORTED', 'TRANSPORT']);\n85:   ctx.on('agent/request-error', async ({ agent, failure, signal }, next) => {\n86:     const code = failure?.code;\n87:     const isOverflow = code === 'CONTEXT_WINDOW_EXCEEDED';\n88:     const isTimeout = TIMEOUT_CODES.has(code);\n89:     if (!isOverflow && !isTimeout) return next();\n90:     // ABORTED with signal.aborted = user cancelled — do not retry\n91:     if (code === 'ABORTED' && signal?.aborted) return next();\n92:     const reason = isOverflow ? 0) + usage.outputTokens;\n117:       if (contextWindow > 0 && total >= contextWindow * 0.8) return true;\n118:     }\n119:     // Fallback heuristic: no usage reported, but message is long and ends abruptly\n120:     if (!usage) {\n121:       const message = eventData?.message;\n122:       const blocks = message?.content;\n123:       if (!Array.isArray(blocks) || blocks.length === 0) return false;\n124:       const lastText = [...blocks].reverse().find((b) => b.type === 'text');\n125:       if (!lastText || !lastText.text || lastText.text.length < 2000) return false;\n126:       const tail = lastText.text.slice(-80);\n127:       const endsProperly = /[.!?。！？\\n`]\\s*$/.test(tail);\n128:       if (!endsProperly) return true;\n129:     }\n130:     return false;\n131:   }\n132: \n133:   ctx.on('session/event', async (session, event) => {\n134:     if (event.type !== 'assistant/message') return;\n135:     if (event.data?.interrupted) return;\n136:     const blocks = event.data?.message?.content;\n137:     if (Array.isArray(blocks) && blocks.some((b) => b.type === 'tool-call')) return;\n138: \n139:     const count = continueCounts.get(session.id) ?? #383 tool/result tool-result "<path>C:\\Users\\spicycorn\\AppData\\Roaming\\npm\\node_modules\\@deepseek-ai\\dsh\\node_modules\\@deepseek-ai\\dsh-agent-preset\\skills\\cordis-plugin-development\\references\\practices.md</path>\n<type>file</type>\n<content>\n1: # Harness plugin practices\n2: \n3: These rules follow from Harness mechanisms. Confirm every Service method, Event name, and dispatch mode named here with `cordis_inspect_query` (`Service`, `Event`) before relying on it; the installed Harness is the authority.\n4: \n5: ## Principles\n6: \n7: 1. **The session log is the only source of truth.** Anything the model sees must be reconstructable from committed session events; fork, resume, and replay derive from the log. Plugin memory is a derived cache.\n8: 2. **Registrations are effects owned by a context.** Plugin unload, agent disposal, slot collapse, and profile patches remove what was registered on the corresponding context. Choose the owning context. A registration on another context, such as `agent.ctx`, has two owners: keep its disposer in your plugin's own effect too, so either teardown removes it.\n9: 3. **The framework drives; the plugin computes.** Session projections, Conversation assembly, and slot rendering subscribe, cache, and publish for you. A plugin that subscribes, rescans, or writes DOM itself bypasses that incremental machinery.\n10: 4. **Extension points are shared; use the weakest mechanism that suffices.** From weakest to strongest: `ctx.tools.restrict()` can only remove tools; `ctx.tools.guard()` can only deny; waterfall listeners can rewrite and depend on registration order; `system-prompt/assemble` replaces the whole assembly. The stronger the mechanism, the more of other plugins' contributions you must preserve.\n11: 5. **Other plugins and other Harness versions read your data.** Unknown event types, older readers, and older cached state meet what you write; declare compatibility with the envelope fields and versions the Harness provides.\n12: 6. **Plugin UI is part of the Harness UI.** Users see one application, so a plugin uses the host's theme tokens, locale, and layout patterns, and matches the look and behavior of host components. Whether that is possible is decided by where the UI renders, so choose the rendering surface before writing any view; later styling inside the wrong surface cannot recover consistency.\n13: \n14: ## Stability\n15: \n16: - A waterfall listener (`agent/pre-step`, `agent/request`, `llm/stream`, `tools/pre-execute`, `tools/execute`, `tools/post-execute`) that does not own the decision must return `next()`. When rewriting an `agent/pre-step` decision, spread it (`{ ...decision, messages }`) so fields such as `startsRequestSeries` survive.\n17: - A denial that must hold regardless of order is a `ctx.tools.guard()`; a guard is synchronous, so a decision that must await something, such as asking the user, returns `ask` from `tools/pre-execute`. Hiding tools from one agent is `ctx.tools.restrict()` on that agent's context; it keeps schema presentation, lookup, and execution aligned. Observe final tool outcomes on `tools/result`; use `tools/post-execute` only to transform a result. Do not listen to `system-prompt/assemble` to add or remove tools or text.\n18: - Add prompt text with `ctx.systemPrompt.section()`. Add per-agent context with `agent.inject()`; it is logged as `agent/inbox/spliced` at call time and enters the next admitted step. `agent/request` listeners cannot change request messages.\n19: - Register per-agent behavior on `agent.ctx`, obtained in an `agent/created` listener, so it is removed when that agent is disposed. Wrap it in one `agent.ctx.effect()` and also keep that disposer, keyed by agent, in your plugin's own effect; unloading the plugin does not dispose `agent.ctx` registrations by itself.\n20: - Put optional services in `inject` or `ctx.inject([...], ...)` so the plugin stays inactive in profiles without them instead of throwing.\n21: - Do not append session events with a new `type`. Readers accept an unknown stored event only when its envelope carries `ignorable: true`, and live `Session.append()` cannot set that marker, so the Session would refuse to reopen. Derive state from existing events, or keep plugin-owned data in a storage service found through inspection.\n22: - Put tunable values in the plugin's `Config` so users change them in `cordis.patch.yml`; the user's patch layer survives upgrades.\n23: \n24: ## Performance\n25: \n26: - Keep per-session state derived from the log in a `ctx.sessionProjections` unit instead of subscribing to `session/event` and rescanning `session.events`. `apply(state, event)` is pure and synchronous and returns the same reference for events it ignores, so unchanged state costs nothing downstream. Read with `stateOf()`. A `view()` returns the same reference when its value is unchanged, which suppresses publication.\n27: - Keep projection state plain JSON and bump `stateVersion` when fields or fold semantics change. The projection cache then checkpoints it, cold reads replay only the tail, and stale checkpoints are discarded.\n28: - Wait on durable events such as `turn/end`, `assistant/message`, or `tool/result`; render live tokens from `agent/assistant-stream`. Do not poll `agent/status`. `whenIdle()` does not mean one follow-up finished: several inputs can share one running interval.\n29: - A timer that starts work calls `agent.followup()`, which wakes the agent; `agent.inject()` does not wake it, so injected context can wait in the inbox until other input arrives. Clear the timer in the owning effect.\n30: \n31: ## UI\n32: \n33: - Render plugin pages as React components in a slot. Do not serve an HTML page from the Host and embed it in an iframe: an iframe document does not receive the host's theme tokens, light/dark switching, or `ctx.locale`.\n34: - Style with the theme tokens that `cordis_inspect_query` `Theme` lists (`--dsw-alias-*`); literal colors are for artwork only. Tokens are the lowest-risk way to match the host: a renamed token degrades appearance but never breaks rendering. Copy spacing, type sizes, and row patterns from an existing host page of the same kind; the Plugin Manager page is the reference for management lists.\n35: - Do not `require('@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives')` or load any other Harness Client package as a module; `dsh.client.inject` entries only order activation and stay allowed. They change without notice, a plain-JS plugin has no type check, and a throwing component blanks your slot entry (console: `slot entry crashed in '<slot>'`). Write your own controls and match the host instead: copy markup, CSS, and behavior from the primitive into the plugin (`src/*.tsx` and `*.module.css` in a DSH source checkout, or the installed package's `lib/index.js` and `lib/**/*.css`), or inspect the rendered host control in the connected page. Rename copied classes under your plugin's prefix, keep only `--dsw-alias-*` token references, and keep the behavior that users rely on, such as Modal focus and Escape handling, `role=\"switch\"` with `aria-checked`, and Tooltip placement. Tokens then remain the only shared styling dependency.\n36: - Contribute through slots: `ctx.slots.inject(ownerKey, () => ctx.slots.register(...))`. The callback's registrations are disposed when the owning declaration collapses and reinstalled when it returns. Read session data through the slot props' selector hooks, subscribing to the smallest slice. Do not write DOM outside your component or append to `document.body`.\n37: - Add a Chat row by registering an event definition with `ctx.uiConversation.events.register()` and its view in the `conversation.chat.node` slot under the definition's `kind`, which is the renderer key; the Conversation layer owns paging, Turn and Step placement, and incremental assembly.\n38: - When the Client needs a value derived from a session, declare `wire.view` on the Host projection. The value reaches the Client already computed; the Client does not fold session events itself.\n\n(End of file - total 38 lines)\n</content>"

'unknown',\n256:         ...(message.name ? { name: message.name } : {}),\n257:         score: density,\n258:         snippet,\n259:       });\n260:     }\n261:   }\n262:   hits.sort((a, b) => (b.score - a.score) || (b.archivedAt - a.archivedAt));\n263:   return { query: q, hits: hits.slice(0, maxHits) };\n264: }\n265: \n266: /**\n267:  * Whether a session has any archived content yet.\n268:  * @param cfg resolved config.\n269:  * @param cwd the session's working directory.\n270:  * @param sessionId owning session id.\n271:  */\n272: export async function hasArchive(cfg, cwd, sessionId) {\n273:   const dir = sessionArchiveDir(cfg, cwd, sessionId);\n274:   try {\n275:     const entries = await readdir(dir);\n276:     return entries.some((f) => f.endsWith('.json'));\n277:   } catch {\n278:     return false;\n279:   }\n280: }\n\n(End of file - total 280 lines)\n</content>"

Give the package and rows unique names; use the Loader's existing YAML syntax, including `!!js` where expressions are needed. Read an existing patch before editing it: a matching override replaces the complete `config`.\n4: \n5: ## Manifest\n6: \n7: A Host-only bundle needs no dependencies, install scripts, or build tool:\n8: \n9: ```json\n10: {\n11:   \"name\": \"@local/my-plugin\",\n12:   \"version\": \"1.0.0\",\n13:   \"private\": true,\n14:   \"type\": \"module\",\n15:   \"exports\": { \".\": \"./index.js\" },\n16:   \"dsh\": { \"bundle\": { \"patch\": \"./cordis.patch.yml\" } }\n17: }\n18: ```\n19: \n20: `cordis.patch.yml`:\n21: \n22: ```yaml\n23: - insert:\n24:     - id: my-plugin\n25:       name: '@local/my-plugin'\n26:       config: {}\n27: ```\n28: \n29: ## Display metadata and icon\n30: \n31: Plugin Manager cards, bundle details, component rows, and the Settings plugin inventory read display text and an icon from the manifest without activating the plugin. Put the title and description in `locale/en.json` (other languages such as `locale/zh.json` use the same fields), and declare the icon as a top-level `icon` in `package.json`:\n32: \n33: ```json\n34: { \"meta\": { \"title\": \"My Decoration\", \"description\": \"Draws a badge under the composer.\" } }\n35: ```\n36: \n37: ```json\n38: {\n39:   \"icon\": \"./icon.svg\",\n40:   \"exports\": { \"./package.json\": \"./package.json\", \"./locale/*.json\": \"./locale/*.json\" },\n41:   \"files\": [\"locale/*.json\", \"icon.svg\"]\n42: }\n43: ```\n44: \n45: `icon` is a path relative to the manifest directory; SVG, PNG, JPEG, and WebP up to 256 KiB are accepted, while absolute paths, URLs, paths outside the directory, and symlinks leaving it are rejected. Missing fields fall back to `package.json` `name` and `description` and to the panel's default artwork; malformed metadata produces a diagnostic and keeps the valid text.\n46: \n47: ## Host plugin export forms\n48: \n49: `index.js` exports one of these forms; do not mix them:\n50: \n51: - `export function apply(ctx, config) {}` with optional `export const inject = ['tools']` and `export const Config`.\n52: - A service class as the default export.\n53: \n54: Register every resource inside `apply` with `ctx.effect` or `ctx.on` and return its cleanup. A plugin that declares `Config` validates the row's `config` at activation; query `Config.listConfigs` for an installed plugin's schema before writing its `config`, and follow `$defs` references in the returned document.\n55: \n56: ## Install, enable, and observe\n57: \n58: `plugin_manager` `install_bundle` performs package installation and bundle selection; do not reproduce those steps with shell commands. Only pass `approvedBuilds` after the user explicitly approves the reported pending build scripts. Preserve returned failures and pending states; report success only after observing the requested capability.\n59: \n60: `list_plugins` and `list_bundles` return exact identifiers for existing installations. `set_plugin` and `set_bundle` toggle them; `remove_bundle` removes a bundle. Inspect saved-state and activation outcomes separately: `failed` requires diagnosis, `overridden` means a higher-priority layer wins, and `restart-required` means the change is not live. Installing a new bundle can activate through HMR; replacing an installed package requires restart to load a fresh JavaScript module generation. Do not infer updated browser code from an unchanged slot id.\n\n(End of file - total 60 lines)\n</content>"

#451 tool/result tool-result "<path>C:\\projects\\dsh_plugins\\dsh-context-sniper\\README.md</path>\n<type>file</type>\n<content>\n1: # dsh-context-sniper\n2: \n3: Lossless context archival + retrieval for DeepSeek Harness.\n4: \n5: When a long conversation causes the local model to timeout during prefill (the\n6: provider reports `pi-ai stream idle timeout`), or overflows the context window\n7: (`CONTEXT_WINDOW_EXCEEDED`), this plugin:\n8: \n9: 1. keeps only the newest **messages** (up to a token budget) in the model surface,\n10: 2. archives the older messages **verbatim** to a durable per-session file (nothing is summarized or lost),\n11: 3. rewrites the surface with one compact marker that tells the model how to get the content back,\n12: 4. authorizes the retry.\n13: \n14: If it cannot free enough context, it falls through to the built-in\n15: `dsh-compaction-basic` summarizer as the safety net. The model retrieves\n16: archived content with the `context_sniper_recall` tool.\n17: \n18: > **English | [中文](README.zh.md)**\n19: \n20: ## Why a separate plugin\n21: \n22: `dsh-compaction-basic` already recovers from overflow — but by *summarizing*\n23: (lossy). This plugin is complementary: it recovers by *archiving* (lossless)\n24: and gives the model a door back into the exact archived text. It does not\n25: modify any DSH base parameter and does not disable the built-in compaction.\n26: \n27: ## What you configure\n28: \n29: Three knobs are user-facing, all editable in **Settings → Context Sniper**\n30: (durable + hot-reloadable):\n31: \n32: - **`surfaceTokenBudget`** — the maximum estimated tokens to keep on the model\n33:   surface. Everything older is archived. This is the *only* budget parameter;\n34:   there is no separate \"default budget\".\n35: - **`maxSearchHits`** — how many archived messages `context_sniper_recall`\n36:   returns per query (1–64, default 8).\n37: - **`hitMaxChars`** — how many characters of each archived message are included\n38:   in a hit (200–20000, default 4000).\n39: \n40: You can also set any of them (plus `pressureRatio`, `archiveDir`, `verbose`)\n41: in the DSH settings document (namespace `dsh-context-sniper`) or in the\n42: composition (`config.*`). Everything has a sane default (see \"Configuration\").\n43: \n44: ## How it works\n45: \n46: Detection is based on the **provider's structured API error response** (HTTP\n47: status + error code). When the LLM API returns a timeout or context-window\n48: failure, the DSH LLM adapter sets `failure.code`; the agent loop then surfaces\n49: it through the `agent/request-error` waterfall.\n50: \n51: This plugin registers the listener with `prepend: true` so it is the\n52: outermost wrapper and acts first:\n53: \n54: - it archives the oldest messages until the surface fits within the token budget,\n55: - returns a terminal `{ kind: \"retry\" }`, so the request re-runs against the\n56:   shrunken context — and the built-in lossy compaction never runs.\n57: \n58: If there is nothing safe to archive (the surface is already minimal), it calls\n59: `next()` and the built-in compaction handles the remainder.\n60: \n61: Optionally, set `pressureRatio` (e.g. `0.8`) to archive *proactively* once\n62: surface tokens cross that fraction of the budget, avoiding the hard failure\n63: entirely. Off by default (`0`).\n64: \n65: ## Archival granularity\n66: \n67: Archival is at **single-message** granularity. The surface is a sequence of\n68: priced nodes (each one a user message, assistant message, or tool result).\n69: The plugin walks from the newest node backwards, accumulating tokens until\n70: the budget is met. Everything older is archived. A tool-pairing safety check\n71: ensures the cut never splits a tool-call from its result.\n72: \n73: ## Marker validity (why trimming no longer corrupts the session)\n74: \n75: When the plugin trims, it appends one compact `user/message` marker carrying\n76: `surfaceOp: { op: 'replace', start, end }` (the same mechanism the built-in\n77: `dsh-compaction` uses) that shadows the archived range in the model surface.\n78: The original events stay in the durable log; only the model-visible surface\n79: changes.\n80: \n81: **The marker's `data.id` is mandatory.** DSH's session-load boundary\n82: (`assertMessageEventShape` in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session`) rejects any\n83: `user/message` whose `data.id` is not a non-empty string, throwing\n84: `session event at seq N lacks an identified message` and making the **whole\n85: session unloadable** (`SessionPersistenceCorruptionError`). Earlier plugin\n86: versions omitted `id`, which is exactly the corruption users saw. This release\n87: always mints a non-empty `id` (the archive UUID) and a `source.kind` of\n88: `plugin`, so every marker round-trips losslessly through DSH persistence and\n89: the session loads cleanly after a trim.\n90: \n91: ### The marker is a directive, not just a notice\n92: \n93: A trim is **not** a session restart — the model should continue the task it was\n94: working on. But an earlier marker only *notified* the model that content had\n95: been archived, so the model often \"restarted\": re-reading files, re-introducing\n96: itself, re-planning — which burns extra tokens and time and can re-overflow the\n97: window. This release makes the marker an explicit instruction to the model:\n98: \n99: - *\"This is a context-archive checkpoint — NOT a session restart. You were\n100:   mid-task; continue exactly where you left off.\"*\n101: - *\"Do not re-read files, re-introduce yourself, or re-plan from scratch.\"*\n102: - *\"If you are missing facts, decisions, file contents, or instructions that\n103:   are no longer visible, call `context_sniper_recall(\"<keyword>\")` to retrieve\n104:   the archived text verbatim.\"*\n105: - *\"Retrieve before you rely on it — do not guess at archived content.\"*\n106: \n107: Because the marker also removes the archived range from the model surface\n108: (`surfaceOp: replace`), the retried request has a **shorter prompt** and a\n109: **faster prefill** — the whole point of trimming. The directive text keeps the\n110: model on-task so it does not undo that speedup by re-exploring.\n111: \n112: ## The recall tool\n113: \n114: `context_sniper_recall(query)` — keyword search over the session's archive.\n115: Returns matching archived messages verbatim (newest first), each with role,\n116: turn, and a snippet. The model should call it whenever it needs facts,\n117: decisions, file contents, or instructions from earlier in the session that\n118: are no longer visible.\n119: \n120: ## Archive format\n121: \n122: One JSON file per archival event, stored **inside the DSH session directory**\n123: so the archive lives alongside the session log it was trimmed from:\n124: \n125: ```\n126: <DSH_HOME>/sessions/<projectKey(cwd)>/<encodeSegment(sessionId)>/context-sniper/<archiveId>.json\n127: ```\n128: \n129: `<projectKey(cwd)>` and `<encodeSegment(sessionId)>` are computed with the\n130: exact same algorithms DSH's `dsh-session-persistence-jsonl` backend uses for\n131: the `session.jsonl.zstd` location, so the archive lands in the very directory\n132: that owns the session. The `context-sniper/` subdirectory is invisible to\n133: DSH's session enumeration (it only treats a directory as a session when it\n134: contains a `session.jsonl[.zstd]` file), so it never interferes with DSH's\n135: storage, listing, or loading.\n136: \n137: Each file contains a single archival record:\n138: \n139: ```jsonc\n140: {\n141:   \"archiveId\": \"…\",\n142:   \"sessionId\": \"…\",\n143:   \"archivedAt\": 1717000000000,\n144:   \"fromSeq\": 3, \"toSeq\": 27,\n145:   \"messageCount\": 15,\n146:   \"freedTokens\": 42000,\n147:   \"budget\": 32768,\n148:   \"reason\": \"timeout\",\n149:   \"messages\": [\n150:     { \"role\": \"user\", \"text\": \"…\" },\n151:     { \"role\": \"assistant\", \"text\": \"…\" },\n152:     { \"role\": \"tool\", \"name\": \"…\", \"text\": \"…\" }\n153:   ]\n154: }\n155: ```\n156: \n157: Each file is small and bounded (one archival event), so the store never\n158: accumulates a single large file.\n159: \n160: ## Settings panel\n161: \n162: Registers a **Settings → Context Sniper** section with:\n163: \n164: - **Surface token budget** — editable. This is the *only* budget parameter:\n165:   it caps how many tokens stay on the model surface. Everything older is\n166:   archived. There is no separate \"default budget\" — the panel no longer shows\n167:   one, to avoid confusion.\n168: - **Recall parameters** — both editable:\n169:   - **Max search hits** (`maxSearchHits`, 1–64): how many archived messages a\n170:     `context_sniper_recall` query returns.\n171:   - **Max chars per hit** (`hitMaxChars`, 200–20000): how many characters of\n172:     each archived message are included in a hit.\n173: - the **archive directory** (read-only, for the active session).\n174: \n175: All three values are durable (persisted via the DSH settings service) and\n176: hot-reloadable — changing them takes effect immediately without a restart.\n177: \n178: ## Configuration\n179: \n180: | Key | Default | Meaning |\n181: |---|---|---|\n182: | `surfaceTokenBudget` | `32768` | Maximum tokens to retain on the model surface. |\n183: | `pressureRatio` | `0` | Proactively archive at this fraction of the budget; `0` = only react to timeout. |\n184: | `maxSearchHits` | `8` | Max archived messages returned per recall query. |\n185: | `hitMaxChars` | `4000` | Max chars of each archived message included in a hit. |\n186: | `archiveDir` | `context-sniper` | Archive subdirectory inside each DSH session directory. |\n187: | `verbose` | `false` | Log every archival decision at info level. |\n188: \n189: ## Install\n190: \n191: ```\n192: dsh plugin --profile web add github:spicycorn/dsh-context-sniper\n193: ```\n194: \n195: This one command installs the package into the profile and **automatically\n196: mounts it** (the `dsh.bundle.patch` field in `package.json` causes the profile\n197: composer to append it to `dsh.profile.bundles` on every boot — no manual edits).\n198: \n199: Restart DSH to activate. Open **Settings → Context Sniper** to verify.\n200: \n201: > **Local development:** first link the peer dependencies, then install by path:\n202: >\n203: > ```\n204: > cd dsh-context-sniper\n205: > node scripts/link-deps.mjs   # creates node_modules links to the DSH profiles\n206: > dsh plugin --profile web add .\n207: > ```\n208: \n209: ## Files\n210: \n211: - `lib/index.js` — host half (detection, archival, recall tool, settings, RPC).\n212: - `lib/select.js` — token-budget selection + lossless surface rewrite.\n213: - `lib/archive.js` — durable archive store (one JSON file per archival event) + keyword search.\n214: - `lib/config.js` — config resolution.\n215: - `lib/client.js` — client half (settings panel).\n216: - `cordis.patch.yml` — mount patch.\n217: \n218: ## Version history\n219: \n220: ### v0.8.1 — compatibility with dsh 0.1.5-rc.3\n221: \n222: **Fixed: the archival path no longer crashes against the current DSH session\n223: API, and it no longer tries to archive the system prompt.**\n224: \n225: The session log surface changed shape in the 0.1.5-rc line, and the plugin's\n226: archival read it through the old accessors. Three fixes, all in `lib/select.js`:\n227: \n228: 1. **`session.events` → `session.eventAt(seq)` / `session.snapshotEvents()`.**\n229:    The current `Session` exposes its log only through `eventAt(seq)` (O(1)\n230:    lookup) and `snapshotEvents()` (a frozen array) — there is no live\n231:    `session.events` array. The archival's per-seq lookups now use\n232:    `eventAt(seq)` and the round-grouping uses `snapshotEvents()`.\n233: 2. **`surfaceOp` field names `start`/`end` → `startSeq`/`endSeq`.** The\n234:    `Session.append('user/message', marker, { surfaceOp: { op: 'replace', … } })`\n235:    replacement contract now names the bounds `startSeq`/`endSeq` (the same as\n236:    the built-in `dsh-compaction-basic` checkpoint writer); the old\n237:    `start`/`end` keys are rejected.\n238: 3. **System-prompt protection.** The token meter prices the rendered system\n239:    prompt (surface node 0) as a node, and the current DSH invariant refuses to\n240:    replace node 0 with a non-system message (\"node 0 holds the system prompt…\").\n241:    The archival now starts at the first *non-system* surface node\n242:    (`firstIdx = systemHead ? 1 : 0`, mirroring `dsh-compaction-basic`) so it\n243:    never archives the prompt, while still never splitting a tool-call/result\n244:    pair.\n245: \n246: `peerDependencies` on the `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` packages are aligned to\n247: `>=0.1.5-rc.1` to match the verified runtime.\n248: \n249: ### v0.8.0 — fixed \"transport failure … HTTP 405\" in the settings panel\n250: \n251: **Bug fixed: the settings panel failed to load config with\n252: `transport failure for /context-sniper/get-state: HTTP 405`.**\n253: \n254: Root cause (DSH 0.1.5 family): the composition mounts `webserver` and\n255: `connection` as **sibling** rows — the `connection` row declares\n256: `inject: [webRuntime]`, and does **not** inject `webServer`. The transport's\n257: own `connection.rpc.handle(channel, handler)` internally calls\n258: `owner.webServer.register(...)`, where `owner` is the **Connection service's own\n259: ctx**. Resolving `webServer` from that ctx walks the ancestor chain, but\n260: `webServer` is a *sibling*, not an ancestor, so the direct property access\n261: throws (\"cannot get property `webServer` without inject\"), the registration is\n262: dropped, and the route is never mounted. The settings panel's POST then falls\n263: through to the static-file fallback (GET-only), which returns **405**. The\n264: `/api` channel works only because it reaches `webServer` through a deferred\n265: `ctx.inject([\"webServer\"], …)` — exactly what the `rpc.handle` path lacks.\n266: \n267: Fix: stop relying on `connection.rpc.handle`. The plugin now **injects\n268: `webServer` itself and registers the `/context-sniper` prefix route directly**\n269: (the same pattern the working host plugin `dsh-better-sidebar` uses), then\n270: answers the identical `client-request` envelope the browser's\n271: `connection.rpc.call` emits — validated with the transport's exported\n272: `clientRequestSchema` and replied as a `server-response`. It also applies the\n273: same Host/Origin + browser-auth fence the `/api` route uses, so the loopback\n274: channel is not exposed to other origins. `peerDependencies` gains\n275: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-connection >=0.1.5-rc.1`.\n276: \n277: > **Note:** the host half is loaded once at DSH process start and is\n278: > ESM-cached, so this fix takes effect on the **next DSH process restart**\n279: > (session switches and `patchReload: live` re-application do not re-execute an\n280: > already-cached host module).\n281: \n282: ### v0.7.0 — compatibility with dsh 0.1.6-alpha.1\n283: \n284: **Adapted to the dsh 0.1.6 settings and connection API.**\n285: \n286: Two breaking changes in the dsh 0.1.6 family required plugin-side updates:\n287: \n288: 1. `@deepseek-ai/dsh-settings` no longer exports the `settingsNamespace()`\n289:    factory. A settings namespace is now a plain string (validated against\n290:    `/^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$/`), passed directly to `settings.register` /\n291:    `settings.get`. The plugin drops the `settingsNamespace` import and uses the\n292:    raw namespace id `'dsh-context-sniper'`.\n293: 2. `connection.rpc.handle(channel, handler)` no longer accepts an options third\n294:    argument. The per-endpoint `{ authority: 'loopback' }` restriction is gone —\n295:    trust and authentication are now applied uniformly by the Connection\n296:    transport. The plugin drops that argument.\n297: \n298: Everything else the plugin touches (events, services, `session.append`/surface,\n299: `defineTool` with `presentCall`, `llm.resolveModelInfo`, `tokenMeter.measure`,\n300: `agents.get`/`followup`) is unchanged in 0.1.6. `peerDependencies` on the\n301: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` packages are raised to `>=0.1.6-alpha.1`.\n302: \n303: ### v0.6.2 — compatibility with dsh 0.1.1-rc.2\n304: \n305: **Bug fixed: output-truncation detection silently stopped firing after the\n306: dsh 0.1.1 update.**\n307: \n308: Root cause: the plugin reads the model's context window to decide that a\n309: completion hit the output cap (it treats a response as truncated when\n310: `input + output ≥ 80%` of the window). It fetched that figure via\n311: `llm.resolveModelInfo(provider, model)`. In dsh 0.1.1-rc.2 that call now\n312: returns the capacity as an **object** — `{ context: { contextWindow } }` —\n313: whereas earlier releases returned a bare number (`{ context: 32768 }`). The\n314: plugin did `contextWindow = info?.context`, so it now held an *object*. The\n315: guard `contextWindow === 0` passed (an object is not `0`), but the real check\n316: `contextWindow > 0 && total >= contextWindow * 0.8` compared an object to a\n317: number (`object > 0` is `false`), so the 80%-of-window rule never fired and\n318: the auto-continue-on-truncation path was dead. The other recovery paths\n319: (timeout/overflow via `agent/request-error`, the recall tool, the settings\n320: panel) were unaffected — everything else the plugin touches in the 0.1.1 API\n321: (events, services, `session.append`/surface, `defineTool`, settings, RPC,\n322: slots) is unchanged.\n323: \n324: Fix:\n325: - read the window from whichever shape is present, so the detector works on\n326:   both the old (number) and new (`{ contextWindow }`) API:\n327:   `typeof context === 'number' ? context : context?.contextWindow`;\n328: - the auto-continue prompt is now sent as a fully-identified message (a stable\n329:   `id`), matching DSH's own `createUserMessage` — the inbox appends it\n330:   verbatim as a `user/message` surface event, and an identified message\n331:   round-trips the session surface and persistence cleanly. Content is\n332:   unchanged.\n333: \n334: ### v0.6.1 — settings now actually persist\n335: \n336: **Bug fixed: every setting reverted to its default on restart.**\n337: \n338: Root cause: the settings schema was built with `z.number().int()`, but the\n339: Schemastery schema library has **no `int()` method** (it exposes `number`,\n340: `natural`, `percent`, plus instance methods `min`/`max`/`step`/`default`). So\n341: `z.object({...})` threw a `TypeError` the moment the plugin registered its\n342: settings namespace; the failure was caught and the owner `scope` stayed `null`.\n343: With `scope` null, the settings panel still updated the in-memory value (so\n344: trimming behaved correctly within the session) but **never wrote anything to the\n345: DSH settings document** — so on the next boot every value fell back to the\n346: composition default. This also explains why `~/.dsh/settings.yaml` had no\n347: `dsh-context-sniper` section at all.\n348: \n349: Fix:\n350: - integer constraints are now expressed with the valid `step(1)` form\n351:   (`z.number().step(1)…`), and the `surfaceTokenBudget` field no longer\n352:   forces a multiple-of-1024 (so any integer ≥ 1024 persists);\n353: - the save RPC handlers now **persist first and only apply the in-memory value\n354:   if the write committed**, and report the real error instead of a false\n355:   \"saved\" — the panel also shows a note when a value applied in-session but\n356:   could not be persisted (degraded mode, no settings service mounted).\n357: \n358: ### v0.6.0\n359: \n360: - Lossless archival + retrieval, timeout/truncation/overflow recovery, recall\n361:   tool, settings panel.\n362: \n363: ## Limitations\n364: \n365: - Keyword search is deterministic substring matching, not semantic — query with\n366:   the terms you actually expect to appear. (A semantic backend such as\n367:   OpenViking can be layered on later without changing this plugin's archive.)\n368: - A single message that exceeds the budget cannot be split; if the entire\n369:   surface is one oversized message, the plugin falls through to built-in\n370:   compaction.\n371: - The token estimates come from the DSH token meter's heuristic (character-based\n372:   pricing), not a real tokenizer. They are conservative approximations.\n\n(End of file - total 372 lines)\n</content>"

#629 tool/result tool-result "<path>C:\\projects\\dsh_plugins\\dsh-context-sniper\\README.zh.md</path>\n<type>file</type>\n<content>\n1: # dsh-context-sniper（上下文狙击手）\n2: \n3: DeepSeek Harness 的**无损上下文归档 + 检索**插件。\n4: \n5: 当长对话导致本地模型 prefill 超时（provider 报告\n6: `pi-ai stream idle timeout`）或撑爆上下文窗口（`CONTEXT_WINDOW_EXCEEDED`）时，\n7: 本插件会：\n8: \n9: 1. 只保留最近的**消息**（至多 token 预算）在模型上下文里；\n10: 2. 把更早的消息**原样**归档到每个会话独立的持久化文件（不做摘要、不丢失）；\n11: 3. 用一条紧凑的\"已归档\"标记替换被移出的内容，并告诉模型如何取回；\n12: 4. 授权重试请求。\n13: \n14: 如果归档后仍不够（或表面已经很小），则回退到内置的 `dsh-compaction-basic`\n15: 做有损摘要兜底。模型通过 `context_sniper_recall` 工具检索归档内容。\n16: \n17: > **[English](README.md) | 中文**\n18: \n19: ## 为什么单独做一个插件\n20: \n21: `dsh-compaction-basic` 已经在做溢出恢复——但靠的是**摘要**（有损）。本插件是互补的：\n22: 靠**归档**（无损）恢复，并给模型一扇回到原文的门。它不改动任何 DSH 底层参数，\n23: 也不会关掉内置压缩。\n24: \n25: ## 你需要配置什么\n26: \n27: 三个参数面向用户，均可在**设置 → Context Sniper** 面板中编辑（持久化 + 热更新）：\n28: \n29: - **`surfaceTokenBudget`**——模型表面保留的最大 token 数，更早的消息全部归档。\n30:   这是**唯一的预算参数**，不存在独立的\"默认 Token 预算\"。\n31: - **`maxSearchHits`**——`context_sniper_recall` 每次查询返回的最大消息条数\n32:   （1–64，默认 8）。\n33: - **`hitMaxChars`**——每条归档消息在命中结果中包含的最大字符数\n34:   （200–20000，默认 4000）。\n35: \n36: 以上任意项（以及 `pressureRatio`、`archiveDir`、`verbose`）也可在 DSH 设置文档\n37: （命名空间 `dsh-context-sniper`）或组合配置（`config.*`）中设置。其余都有合理\n38: 默认值（见\"配置\"）。\n39: \n40: ## 如何工作\n41: \n42: 识别基于 **provider 的结构化 API 错误响应**。当 LLM API 返回超时或\n43: 上下文窗口溢出错误时，DSH 的 LLM adapter 设置 `failure.code`，agent 循环\n44: 通过 `agent/request-error` 瀑布将其暴露。\n45: \n46: 本插件以 `prepend: true` 注册该监听器，使其成为最外层包裹、最先行动：\n47: \n48: - 从最旧消息开始归档，直到表面 token ≤ 预算；\n49: - 返回终结动作 `{ kind: \"retry\" }`，请求随即针对收缩后的上下文重跑——\n50:   内置有损压缩因此不会执行。\n51: \n52: 若没有可安全归档的内容（表面已最小），则调用 `next()`，交给内置压缩兜底。\n53: \n54: 可选：设置 `pressureRatio`（如 `0.8`），在表面 token 超过预算该比例时**提前**\n55: 归档，避免硬失败。默认关闭（`0`）。\n56: \n57: ## 归档粒度\n58: \n59: 归档以**单条消息**为单位。表面是一组带 token 定价的节点（每条 user message、\n60: assistant message 或 tool result）。插件从最新节点向前累加 token，达到预算时\n61: 停止，更早的全部归档。工具调用配对安全检查确保切割不会把 tool-call 和\n62: 其 result 拆散。\n63: \n64: ## 标记合法性（为什么裁剪不再破坏会话）\n65: \n66: 裁剪时，本插件追加一条紧凑的 `user/message` 标记，携带\n67: `surfaceOp: { op: 'replace', start, end }`（与内置 `dsh-compaction` 同一机制），\n68: 在模型表面上\"影子化\"被归档的范围。原始事件仍保留在持久化日志中，\n69: 改变的只是模型可见的表面。\n70: \n71: **标记的 `data.id` 是必填项。** DSH 的会话加载边界（`@deepseek-ai/dsh-session`\n72: 的 `assertMessageEventShape`）会拒绝任何 `data.id` 不是非空字符串的 `user/message`，\n73: 抛出 `session event at seq N lacks an identified message`，并导致**整个会话无法加载**\n74: （`SessionPersistenceCorruptionError`）。早期插件版本省略了 `id`，这正是用户看到的\n75: 损坏。本版本始终生成非空 `id`（归档 UUID）并设置 `source.kind` 为 `plugin`，\n76: 因此每条标记都能无损地通过 DSH 持久化往返，裁剪后会话也能正常加载。\n77: \n78: ### 标记是指令，不只是提示\n79: \n80: 裁剪**不是**重开会话——模型应该继续它正在做的任务。但早期标记只是*通知*模型\n81: 内容被归档了，模型于是经常\"重启\"：重新读文件、重新自我介绍、重新规划——\n82: 消耗额外 token 和时间，甚至再次撑爆窗口。本版本把标记变成对模型的明确指令：\n83: \n84: - *\"这是一个上下文归档检查点——不是会话重启。你正在任务中途，请从你停下的地方\n85:   继续。\"*\n86: - *\"不要重新读文件、不要重新自我介绍、不要从头重新规划。\"*\n87: - *\"如果你缺少已不可见的事实、决策、文件内容或指令，调用\n88:   `context_sniper_recall(\"<关键词>\")` 检索归档原文。\"*\n89: - *\"先检索再依赖——不要凭猜测使用归档内容。\"*\n90: \n91: 由于标记同时通过 `surfaceOp: replace` 把被归档范围从模型表面移除，重试请求的\n92: **prompt 更短、prefill 更快**——这正是裁剪的意义。指令文本让模型保持在任务上，\n93: 不会通过重新探索来抵消这个加速。\n94: \n95: ## 归档存储位置（与 DSH 会话目录对齐）\n96: \n97: 每次归档一个 JSON 文件，存放在 **DSH 会话目录内**，使其与被裁剪的会话日志\n98: 同处一目录：\n99: \n100: ```\n101: <DSH_HOME>/sessions/<projectKey(cwd)>/<encodeSegment(sessionId)>/context-sniper/<archiveId>.json\n102: ```\n103: \n104: `<projectKey(cwd)>` 与 `<encodeSegment(sessionId)>` 使用 DSH\n105: `dsh-session-persistence-jsonl` 后端定位 `session.jsonl.zstd` 的**同一套算法**计算，\n106: 因此归档落在拥有该会话的同一目录中。`context-sniper/` 子目录对 DSH 的会话枚举\n107: 不可见（DSH 只把包含 `session.jsonl[.zstd]` 文件的目录当作会话），因此绝不会\n108: 干扰 DSH 的存储、列表或加载。\n109: \n110: ## 检索工具\n111: \n112: `context_sniper_recall(query)`——对当前会话的归档做关键词检索，按原文返回匹配的消息\n113: （最新在前），每条带角色、轮次与片段。模型在需要本会话早期、已不可见的事实、决策、\n114: 文件内容或指令时调用它。\n115: \n116: ## 配置\n117: \n118: | 键 | 默认 | 含义 |\n119: |---|---|---|\n120: | `surfaceTokenBudget` | `32768` | 模型表面保留的最大 token 数。 |\n121: | `pressureRatio` | `0` | 在预算该比例处提前归档；`0` = 仅在超时时反应。 |\n122: | `maxSearchHits` | `8` | 每次检索返回的最大归档消息数。 |\n123: | `hitMaxChars` | `4000` | 每条命中消息的最大字符数。 |\n124: | `archiveDir` | `context-sniper` | 每个 DSH 会话目录内的归档子目录。 |\n125: | `verbose` | `false` | 以 info 级别记录每次归档决策。 |\n126: \n127: ## 安装\n128: \n129: ```\n130: dsh plugin --profile web add github:spicycorn/dsh-context-sniper\n131: ```\n132: \n133: ## 文件\n134: \n135: - `lib/index.js` — 宿主半（检测、归档、检索工具、设置、RPC）。\n136: - `lib/select.js` — token 预算选择 + 无损表面重写。\n137: - `lib/archive.js` — 持久化归档存储（每次归档一个独立 JSON 文件）+ 关键词检索。\n138: - `lib/config.js` — 配置解析。\n139: - `lib/client.js` — 客户端半（设置面板）。\n140: - `cordis.patch.yml` — 挂载补丁。\n141: \n142: ## 版本历史\n143: \n144: ### v0.8.1 — 适配 dsh 0.1.5-rc.3\n145: \n146: **修复：归档路径不再因当前 DSH 的 session API 变更而崩溃，且不再尝试归档系统提示词。**\n147: \n148: 0.1.5-rc 一族的 session 日志表面改变了形态，而插件的归档仍用旧接口读取。三处修复，\n149: 全在 `lib/select.js`：\n150: \n151: 1. **`session.events` → `session.eventAt(seq)` / `session.snapshotEvents()`。**\n152:    当前 `Session` 只通过 `eventAt(seq)`（O(1) 查单条）和 `snapshotEvents()`（冻结数组）\n153:    暴露日志，**没有** `session.events` 这个活数组。归档的按 seq 查找改用\n154:    `eventAt(seq)`，轮次分组改用 `snapshotEvents()`。\n155: 2. **`surfaceOp` 字段名 `start`/`end` → `startSeq`/`endSeq`。**\n156:    `Session.append('user/message', marker, { surfaceOp: { op: 'replace', … } })`\n157:    的替换契约现在把边界命名为 `startSeq`/`endSeq`（与内置 `dsh-compaction-basic`\n158:    的检查点写法一致）；旧的 `start`/`end` 会被拒绝。\n159: 3. **系统提示词保护。** token 计量器会把渲染出的系统提示词（表面节点 0）计入节点，\n160:    而当前 DSH 的不变量拒绝用非 system 消息替换节点 0（\"node 0 holds the system\n161:    prompt…\"）。归档现在从**第一个非 system 表面节点**开始\n162:    （`firstIdx = systemHead ? 1 : 0`，与 `dsh-compaction-basic` 一致），\n163:    因此永不归档系统提示词，同时仍不会拆散 tool-call/result 配对。\n164: \n165: `peerDependencies` 里的 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` 包对齐到 `>=0.1.5-rc.1`，与实测运行时一致。\n166: \n167: ### v0.8.0 — 修复设置面板 \"transport failure … HTTP 405\"\n168: \n169: **修复的 Bug：设置面板加载配置时报\n170: `无法加载配置: transport failure for /context-sniper/get-state: HTTP 405`。**\n171: \n172: 根本原因（DSH 0.1.5 一族）：组合配置把 `webserver` 与 `connection` 挂成**兄弟\n173: 行**——`connection` 行 `inject: [webRuntime]`，**并不注入 `webServer`**。而\n174: `connection.rpc.handle(channel, handler)` 内部调用\n175: `owner.webServer.register(...)`，其中 `owner` 是 **Connection 服务自身的 ctx**。\n176: 从那个 ctx 走 `webServer` 时，`webServer` 是*兄弟*而不是*祖先*，直接属性访问\n177: 解析不到（\"cannot get property webServer without inject\"），注册因此抛错、路由\n178: 从未挂载。设置面板的 POST 落到静态文件回退（只放行 GET），于是返回 **405**。\n179: `/api` 通道之所以正常，是因为它内部走 `ctx.inject([\"webServer\"], ...)` 延迟注入\n180: 才拿到 `webServer`——这正是 `rpc.handle` 这条路径缺的东西。\n181: \n182: 修复：不再依赖 `connection.rpc.handle`，改为**直接注入 The model retrieves\\narchived content with the `context_sniper_recall` tool.\\n\\n> **English | [中文](README.zh.md)**\\n\\nWorks with **DSH 0.2.0-rc.1+** (verified against 0.2.0-rc.1 / rc.2).\\n\\n## Why a separate plugin\\n\\n`dsh-compaction-basic` already recovers from overflow — but by *summarizing*\\n(lossy). This plugin is complementary: it recovers by *archiving* (lossless)\\nand gives the model a door back into the exact archived text. It does not\\nmodify any DSH base parameter and does not disable the built-in compaction.\\n\\n## What you configure\\n\\nThree knobs are user-facing, all editable in **Settings → Context Sniper**\\n(live-saved through the DSH settings mirror — durable, hot-reloadable, no\\nrestart):\\n\\n- **`surfaceTokenBudget`** — the maximum estimated tokens to keep on the model\\n  surface. Everything older is archived. This is the *only* budget parameter;\\n  there is no separate \\\"default budget\\\".\\n- **`maxSearchHits`** — how many archived messages `context_sniper_recall`\\n  returns per query (1–64, default 8).\\n- **`hitMaxChars`** — how many characters of each archived message are included\\n  in a hit (200–20000, default 4000).\\n\\nYou can also set any of them (plus `pressureRatio`, `archiveDir`, `verbose`)\\nin the DSH settings document (namespace `dsh-context-sniper`) or in the\\ncomposition (`config.*`). Everything has a sane default (see \\\"Configuration\\\").\\n\\n## How it works\\n\\nDetection is based on the **provider's structured API error response** (HTTP\\nstatus + error code). When the LLM API returns a timeout or context-window\\nfailure, the DSH LLM adapter sets `failure.code`; the agent loop then surfaces\\nit through the `agent/request-error` waterfall.\\n\\nThis plugin registers the listener with `prepend: true` so it is the\\noutermost wrapper and acts first:\\n\\n- it archives the oldest messages until the surface fits within the token budget,\\n- returns a terminal `{ kind: \\\"retry\\\" }`, so the request re-runs against the\\n  shrunken context — and the built-in lossy compaction never runs.\\n\\nIf there is nothing safe to archive (the surface is already minimal), it calls\\n`next()` and the built-in compaction handles the remainder. A cancelled\\nrequest (`signal.aborted`) is never retried.\\n\\nOptionally, set `pressureRatio` (e.g. `0.8`) to archive *proactively* once\\nsurface tokens cross that fraction of the budget, avoiding the hard failure\\nentirely. Off by default (`0`).\\n\\n## Archival granularity\\n\\nArchival is at **single-message** granularity. The surface is a sequence of\\npriced nodes (each one a user message, assistant message, or tool result).\\nThe plugin walks from the newest node backwards, accumulating tokens until\\nthe budget is met. Everything older is archived. A tool-pairing safety check\\nensures the cut never splits a tool-call from its result.\\n\\n## Marker validity (why trimming no longer corrupts the session)\\n\\nWhen the plugin trims, it appends one compact `user/message` marker carrying\\n`surfaceOp: { op: 'replace', startSeq, endSeq }` (the same mechanism the\\nbuilt-in `dsh-compaction-basic` uses) that shadows the archived range in the\\nmodel surface. The original events stay in the durable log; only the\\nmodel-visible surface changes.\\n\\n**The marker's `data.id` is mandatory.** DSH's session-load boundary\\n(`assertMessageEventShape` in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session`) rejects any\\n`user/message` whose `data.id` is not a non-empty string, throwing\\n`session event at seq N lacks an identified message` and making the **whole\\nsession unloadable** (`SessionPersistenceCorruptionError`). Earlier plugin\\nversions omitted `id`, which is exactly the corruption users saw. This release\\nalways mints a non-empty `id` (the archive UUID) and a `source.kind` of\\n`plugin`, so every marker round-trips losslessly through DSH persistence and\\nthe session loads cleanly after a trim.\\n\\n### The marker is a directive, not just a notice\\n\\nA trim is **not** a session restart — the model should continue the task it was\\nworking on. But an earlier marker only *notified* the model that content had\\nbeen archived, so the model often \\\"restarted\\\": re-reading files, re-introducing\\nitself, re-planning — which burns extra tokens and time and can re-overflow the\\nwindow. This release makes the marker an explicit instruction to the model:\\n\\n- *\\\"This is a context-archive checkpoint — NOT a session restart. You were\\n  mid-task; continue exactly where you left off.\\\"*\\n- *\\\"Do not re-read files, re-introduce yourself, or re-plan from scratch.\\\"*\\n- *\\\"If you are missing facts, decisions, file contents, or instructions that\\n  are no longer visible, call `context_sniper_recall(\\\"<keyword>\\\")` to retrieve\\n  the archived text verbatim.\\\"*\\n- *\\\"Retrieve before you rely on it — do not guess at archived content.\\\"*\\n\\nBecause the marker also removes the archived range from the model surface\\n(`surfaceOp: replace`), the retried request has a **shorter prompt** and a\\n**faster prefill** — the whole point of trimming. The directive text keeps the\\nmodel on-task so it does not undo that speedup by re-exploring.\\n\\n## The recall tool\\n\\n`context_sniper_recall(query)` — keyword search over the session's archive.\\nReturns matching archived messages verbatim (newest first), each with role,\\nturn, and a snippet. The model should call it whenever it needs facts,\\ndecisions, file contents, or instructions from earlier in the session that\\nare no longer visible.\\n\\n## Archive format\\n\\nOne JSON file per archival event, stored **inside the DSH session directory**\\nso the archive lives alongside the session log it was trimmed from:\\n\\n```\\n<DSH_HOME>/sessions/<projectKey(cwd)>/<encodeSegment(sessionId)>/context-sniper/<archiveId>.json\\n```\\n\\n`<projectKey(cwd)>` and `<encodeSegment(sessionId)>` are computed with the\\nexact same algorithms DSH's `dsh-session-persistence-jsonl` backend uses for\\nthe `session.jsonl.zstd` location, so the archive lands in the very directory\\nthat owns the session. The `context-sniper/` subdirectory is invisible to\\nDSH's session enumeration (it only treats a directory as a session when it\\ncontains a `session.jsonl[.zstd]` file), so it never interferes with DSH's\\nstorage, listing, or loading.\\n\\nEach file contains a single archival record:\\n\\n```jsonc\\n{\\n  \\\"archiveId\\\": \\\"…\\\",\\n  \\\"sessionId\\\": \\\"…\\\",\\n  \\\"archivedAt\\\": 1717000000000,\\n  \\\"fromSeq\\\": 3, \\\"toSeq\\\": 27,\\n  \\\"messageCount\\\": 15,\\n  \\\"freedTokens\\\": 42000,\\n  \\\"budget\\\": 32768,\\n  \\\"reason\\\": \\\"timeout\\\",\\n  \\\"messages\\\": [\\n    { \\\"role\\\": \\\"user\\\", \\\"text\\\": \\\"…\\\" },\\n    { \\\"role\\\": \\\"assistant\\\", \\\"text\\\": \\\"…\\\" },\\n    { \\\"role\\\": \\\"tool\\\", \\\"name\\\": \\\"…\\\", \\\"text\\\": \\\"…\\\" }\\n  ]\\n}\\n```\\n\\nEach file is small and bounded (one archival event), so the store never\\naccumulates a single large file.\\n\\n## Settings panel\\n\\nRegisters a **Settings → Context Sniper** section (zh/en localized, theme\\ntokens only — it follows light/dark automatically):\\n\\n- **Settings card** — the three editable values above, read and written\\n  **live** through the shared settings mirror (`ctx.configForms`): every edit\\n  is validated, revision-fenced, and persisted immediately; a per-field\\n  **Reset** clears the override back to the composition default. Three fixes, all in `lib/select.js`:\\n\\n1. **`session.events` → `session.eventAt(seq)` / `session.snapshotEvents()`.**\\n   The current `Session` exposes its log only through `eventAt(seq)` (O(1)\\n   lookup) and `snapshotEvents()` (a frozen array) — there is no live\\n   `session.events` array. The transport's\\nown `connection.rpc.handle(channel, handler)` internally calls\\n`owner.webServer.register(...)`, where `owner` is the **Connection service's own\\nctx**. Resolving `webServer` from that ctx walks the ancestor chain, but\\n`webServer` is a *sibling*, not an ancestor, so the direct property access\\nthrows (\\\"cannot get property `webServer` without inject\\\"), the registration is\\ndropped, and the route is never mounted. The settings panel's POST then falls\\nthrough to the static-file fallback (GET-only), which returns **405**. The\\n`/api` channel works only because it reaches `webServer` through a deferred\\n`ctx.inject([\\\"webServer\\\"], …)` — exactly what the `rpc.handle` path lacks.\\n\\nFix: stop relying on `connection.rpc.handle`. The plugin now **injects\\n`webServer` itself and registers the `/context-sniper` prefix route directly**\\n(the same pattern the working host plugin `dsh-better-sidebar` uses), then\\nanswers the identical `client-request` envelope the browser's\\n`connection.rpc.call` emits — validated with the transport's exported\\n`clientRequestSchema` and replied as a `server-response`. It also applies the\\nsame Host/Origin + browser-auth fence the `/api` route uses, so the loopback\\nchannel is not exposed to other origins.\\n\\n> **Note:** the host half is loaded once at DSH process start and is\\n> ESM-cached, so this fix takes effect on the **next DSH process restart**\\n> (session switches and `patchReload: live` re-application do not re-execute an\\n> already-cached host module).\\n\\n### v0.7.0 — compatibility with dsh 0.1.6-alpha.1\\n\\n**Adapted to the dsh 0.1.6 settings and connection API.**\\n\\nTwo breaking changes in the dsh 0.1.6 family required plugin-side updates:\\n\\n1. `@deepseek-ai/dsh-settings` no longer exports the `settingsNamespace()`\\n   factory. A settings namespace is now a plain string (validated against\\n   `/^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$/`), passed directly to `settings.register` /\\n   `settings.get`. The plugin drops the `settingsNamespace` import and uses the\\n   raw namespace id `'dsh-context-sniper'`.\\n2. `connection.rpc.handle(channel, handler)` no longer accepts an options third\\n   argument. The per-endpoint `{ authority: 'loopback' }` restriction is gone —\\n   trust and authentication are now applied uniformly by the Connection\\n   transport. The plugin drops that argument.\\n\\n### v0.6.2 — compatibility with dsh 0.1.1-rc.2\\n\\n**Bug fixed: output-truncation detection silently stopped firing after the\\ndsh 0.1.1 update.**\\n\\nRoot cause: the plugin reads the model's context window to decide that a\\ncompletion hit the output cap (it treats a response as truncated when\\n`input + output ≥ 80%` of the window). It fetched that figure via\\n`llm.resolveModelInfo(provider, model)`. In dsh 0.1.1-rc.2 that call now\\nreturns the capacity as an **object** — `{ context: { contextWindow } }` —\\nwhereas earlier releases returned a bare number (`{ context: 32768 }`). #638 tool/call tool/call {"turn":1,"step":106,"callId":"call_c7c38f882007419c981bc4cf","name":"write","arguments":"{\"content\":\"# dsh-context-sniper\\n\\nLossless context archival + retrieval for DeepSeek Harness.\\n\\nWhen a long conversation causes the local model to timeout during prefill (the\\nprovider reports `pi-ai stream idle timeout`), or overflows the context window\\n(`CONTEXT_WINDOW_EXCEEDED`), this plugin:\\n\\n1. keeps only the newest **messages** (up to a token budget) in the model surface,\\n2. archives the older messages **verbatim** to a durable per-session file (nothing is summarized or lost),\\n3. rewrites the surface with one compact marker that tells the model how to get the content back,\\n4. authorizes the retry.\\n\\nIf it cannot free enough context, it falls through to the built-in\\n`dsh-compaction-basic` summarizer as the safety net. The model retrieves\\narchived content with the `context_sniper_recall` tool.\\n\\n> **English | [中文](README.zh.md)**\\n\\nWorks with **DSH 0.2.0-rc.1+** (verified against 0.2.0-rc.1 / rc.2).\\n\\n## Why a separate plugin\\n\\n`dsh-compaction-basic` already recovers from overflow — but by *summarizing*\\n(lossy). This plugin is complementary: it recovers by *archiving* (lossless)\\nand gives the model a door back into the exact archived text. It does not\\nmodify any DSH base parameter and does not disable the built-in compaction.\\n\\n## What you configure\\n\\nThree knobs are user-facing, all editable in **Settings → Context Sniper**\\n(live-saved through the DSH settings mirror — durable, hot-reloadable, no\\nrestart):\\n\\n- **`surfaceTokenBudget`** — the maximum estimated tokens to keep on the model\\n  surface. Everything older is archived. This is the *only* budget parameter;\\n  there is no separate \\\"default budget\\\".\\n- **`maxSearchHits`** — how many archived messages `context_sniper_recall`\\n  returns per query (1–64, default 8).\\n- **`hitMaxChars`** — how many characters of each archived message are included\\n  in a hit (200–20000, default 4000).\\n\\nYou can also set any of them (plus `pressureRatio`, `archiveDir`, `verbose`)\\nin the DSH settings document (namespace `dsh-context-sniper`) or in the\\ncomposition (`config.*`). Everything has a sane default (see \\\"Configuration\\\").\\n\\n## How it works\\n\\nDetection is based on the **provider's structured API error response** (HTTP\\nstatus + error code). When the LLM API returns a timeout or context-window\\nfailure, the DSH LLM adapter sets `failure.code`; the agent loop then surfaces\\nit through the `agent/request-error` waterfall.\\n\\nThis plugin registers the listener with `prepend: true` so it is the\\noutermost wrapper and acts first:\\n\\n- it archives the oldest messages until the surface fits within the token budget,\\n- returns a terminal `{ kind: \\\"retry\\\" }`, so the request re-runs against the\\n  shrunken context — and the built-in lossy compaction never runs.\\n\\nIf there is nothing safe to archive (the surface is already minimal), it calls\\n`next()` and the built-in compaction handles the remainder. A cancelled\\nrequest (`signal.aborted`) is never retried.\\n\\nOptionally, set `pressureRatio` (e.g. `0.8`) to archive *proactively* once\\nsurface tokens cross that fraction of the budget, avoiding the hard failure\\nentirely. Off by default (`0`).\\n\\n## Archival granularity\\n\\nArchival is at **single-message** granularity. The surface is a sequence of\\npriced nodes (each one a user message, assistant message, or tool result).\\nThe plugin walks from the newest node backwards, accumulating tokens until\\nthe budget is met. Everything older is archived. A tool-pairing safety check\\nensures the cut never splits a tool-call from its result.\\n\\n## Marker validity (why trimming no longer corrupts the session)\\n\\nWhen the plugin trims, it appends one compact `user/message` marker carrying\\n`surfaceOp: { op: 'replace', startSeq, endSeq }` (the same mechanism the\\nbuilt-in `dsh-compaction-basic` uses) that shadows the archived range in the\\nmodel surface. The original events stay in the durable log; only the\\nmodel-visible surface changes.\\n\\n**The marker's `data.id` is mandatory.** DSH's session-load boundary\\n(`assertMessageEventShape` in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session`) rejects any\\n`user/message` whose `data.id` is not a non-empty string, throwing\\n`session event at seq N lacks an identified message` and making the **whole\\nsession unloadable** (`SessionPersistenceCorruptionError`). Earlier plugin\\nversions omitted `id`, which is exactly the corruption users saw. This release\\nalways mints a non-empty `id` (the archive UUID) and a `source.kind` of\\n`plugin`, so every marker round-trips losslessly through DSH persistence and\\nthe session loads cleanly after a trim.\\n\\n### The marker is a directive, not just a notice\\n\\nA trim is **not** a session restart — the model should continue the task it was\\nworking on. But an earlier marker only *notified* the model that content had\\nbeen archived, so the model often \\\"restarted\\\": re-reading files, re-introducing\\nitself, re-planning — which burns extra tokens and time and can re-overflow the\\nwindow. This release makes the marker an explicit instruction to the model:\\n\\n- *\\\"This is a context-archive checkpoint — NOT a session restart. You were\\n  mid-task; continue exactly where you left off.\\\"*\\n- *\\\"Do not re-read files, re-introduce yourself, or re-plan from scratch.\\\"*\\n- *\\\"If you are missing facts, decisions, file contents, or instructions that\\n  are no longer visible, call `context_sniper_recall(\\\"<keyword>\\\")` to retrieve\\n  the archived text verbatim.\\\"*\\n- *\\\"Retrieve before you rely on it — do not guess at archived content.\\\"*\\n\\nBecause the marker also removes the archived range from the model surface\\n(`surfaceOp: replace`), the retried request has a **shorter prompt** and a\\n**faster prefill** — the whole point of trimming. The directive text keeps the\\nmodel on-task so it does not undo that speedup by re-exploring.\\n\\n## The recall tool\\n\\n`context_sniper_recall(query)` — keyword search over the session's archive.\\nReturns matching archived messages verbatim (newest first), each with role,\\nturn, and a snippet. The model should call it whenever it needs facts,\\ndecisions, file contents, or instructions from earlier in the session that\\nare no longer visible.\\n\\n## Archive format\\n\\nOne JSON file per archival event, stored **inside the DSH session directory**\\nso the archive lives alongside the session log it was trimmed from:\\n\\n```\\n<DSH_HOME>/sessions/<projectKey(cwd)>/<encodeSegment(sessionId)>/context-sniper/<archiveId>.json\\n```\\n\\n`<projectKey(cwd)>` and `<encodeSegment(sessionId)>` are computed with the\\nexact same algorithms DSH's `dsh-session-persistence-jsonl` backend uses for\\nthe `session.jsonl.zstd` location, so the archive lands in the very directory\\nthat owns the session. The `context-sniper/` subdirectory is invisible to\\nDSH's session enumeration (it only treats a directory as a session when it\\ncontains a `session.jsonl[.zstd]` file), so it never interferes with DSH's\\nstorage, listing, or loading.\\n\\nEach file contains a single archival record:\\n\\n```jsonc\\n{\\n  \\\"archiveId\\\": \\\"…\\\",\\n  \\\"sessionId\\\": \\\"…\\\",\\n  \\\"archivedAt\\\": 1717000000000,\\n  \\\"fromSeq\\\": 3, \\\"toSeq\\\": 27,\\n  \\\"messageCount\\\": 15,\\n  \\\"freedTokens\\\": 42000,\\n  \\\"budget\\\": 32768,\\n  \\\"reason\\\": \\\"timeout\\\",\\n  \\\"messages\\\": [\\n    { \\\"role\\\": \\\"user\\\", \\\"text\\\": \\\"…\\\" },\\n    { \\\"role\\\": \\\"assistant\\\", \\\"text\\\": \\\"…\\\" },\\n    { \\\"role\\\": \\\"tool\\\", \\\"name\\\": \\\"…\\\", \\\"text\\\": \\\"…\\\" }\\n  ]\\n}\\n```\\n\\nEach file is small and bounded (one archival event), so the store never\\naccumulates a single large file.\\n\\n## Settings panel\\n\\nRegisters a **Settings → Context Sniper** section (zh/en localized, theme\\ntokens only — it follows light/dark automatically):\\n\\n- **Settings card** — the three editable values above, read and written\\n  **live** through the shared settings mirror (`ctx.configForms`): every edit\\n  is validated, revision-fenced, and persisted immediately; a per-field\\n  **Reset** clears the override back to the composition default. #706 tool/result tool-result "<path>C:\\projects\\dsh_plugins\\dsh-context-sniper\\README.md</path>\n<type>file</type>\n<content>\n1: # dsh-context-sniper\n2: \n3: Lossless context archival + retrieval for DeepSeek Harness.\n4: \n5: When a long conversation causes the local model to timeout during prefill (the\n6: provider reports `pi-ai stream idle timeout`), or overflows the context window\n7: (`CONTEXT_WINDOW_EXCEEDED`), this plugin:\n8: \n9: 1. keeps only the newest **messages** (up to a token budget) in the model surface,\n10: 2. archives the older messages **verbatim** to a durable per-session file (nothing is summarized or lost),\n11: 3. rewrites the surface with one compact marker that tells the model how to get the content back,\n12: 4. authorizes the retry.\n13: \n14: If it cannot free enough context, it falls through to the built-in\n15: `dsh-compaction-basic` summarizer as the safety net. The model retrieves\n16: archived content with the `context_sniper_recall` tool.\n17: \n18: > **English | [中文](README.zh.md)**\n19: \n20: ## Why a separate plugin\n21: \n22: `dsh-compaction-basic` already recovers from overflow — but by *summarizing*\n23: (lossy). This plugin is complementary: it recovers by *archiving* (lossless)\n24: and gives the model a door back into the exact archived text. It does not\n25: modify any DSH base parameter and does not disable the built-in compaction.\n26: \n27: ## What you configure\n28: \n29: Three knobs are user-facing, all editable in **Settings → Context Sniper**\n30: (durable + hot-reloadable):\n31: \n32: - **`surfaceTokenBudget`** — the maximum estimated tokens to keep on the model\n33:   surface. Everything older is archived. This is the *only* budget parameter;\n34:   there is no separate \"default budget\".\n35: - **`maxSearchHits`** — how many archived messages `context_sniper_recall`\n36:   returns per query (1–64, default 8).\n37: - **`hitMaxChars`** — how many characters of each archived message are included\n38:   in a hit (200–20000, default 4000).\n39: \n40: You can also set any of them (plus `pressureRatio`, `archiveDir`, `verbose`)\n41: in the DSH settings document (namespace `dsh-context-sniper`) or in the\n42: composition (`config.*`). Everything has a sane default (see \"Configuration\").\n43: \n44: ## How it works\n45: \n46: Detection is based on the **provider's structured API error response** (HTTP\n47: status + error code). When the LLM API returns a timeout or context-window\n48: failure, the DSH LLM adapter sets `failure.code`; the agent loop then surfaces\n49: it through the `agent/request-error` waterfall.\n50: \n51: This plugin registers the listener with `prepend: true` so it is the\n52: outermost wrapper and acts first:\n53: \n54: - it archives the oldest messages until the surface fits within the token budget,\n55: - returns a terminal `{ kind: \"retry\" }`, so the request re-runs against the\n56:   shrunken context — and the built-in lossy compaction never runs.\n57: \n58: If there is nothing safe to archive (the surface is already minimal), it calls\n59: `next()` and the built-in compaction handles the remainder.\n60: \n61: Optionally, set `pressureRatio` (e.g. `0.8`) to archive *proactively* once\n62: surface tokens cross that fraction of the budget, avoiding the hard failure\n63: entirely. Off by default (`0`).\n64: \n65: ## Archival granularity\n66: \n67: Archival is at **single-message** granularity. The surface is a sequence of\n68: priced nodes (each one a user message, assistant message, or tool result).\n69: The plugin walks from the newest node backwards, accumulating tokens until\n70: the budget is met. Everything older is archived. A tool-pairing safety check\n71: ensures the cut never splits a tool-call from its result.\n72: \n73: ## Marker validity (why trimming no longer corrupts the session)\n74: \n75: When the plugin trims, it appends one compact `user/message` marker carrying\n76: `surfaceOp: { op: 'replace', start, end }` (the same mechanism the built-in\n77: `dsh-compaction` uses) that shadows the archived range in the model surface.\n78: The original events stay in the durable log; only the model-visible surface\n79: changes.\n80: \n81: **The marker's `d\n\n[... tool result middle pruned ...]\n\n the write committed**, and report the real error instead of a false\n355:   \"saved\" — the panel also shows a note when a value applied in-session but\n356:   could not be persisted (degraded mode, no settings service mounted).\n357: \n358: ### v0.6.0\n359: \n360: - Lossless archival + retrieval, timeout/truncation/overflow recovery, recall\n361:   tool, settings panel.\n362: \n363: ## Limitations\n364: \n365: - Keyword search is deterministic substring matching, not semantic — query with\n366:   the terms you actually expect to appear. (A semantic backend such as\n367:   OpenViking can be layered on later without changing this plugin's archive.)\n368: - A single message that exceeds the budget cannot be split; if the entire\n369:   surface is one oversized message, the plugin falls through to built-in\n370:   compaction.\n371: - The token estimates come from the DSH token meter's heuristic (character-based\n372:   pricing), not a real tokenizer. They are conservative approximations.\n\n(End of file - total 372 lines)\n</content>"

#708 tool/result tool-result "<path>C:\\projects\\dsh_plugins\\dsh-context-sniper\\README.zh.md</path>\n<type>file</type>\n<content>\n1: # dsh-context-sniper（上下文狙击手）\n2: \n3: DeepSeek Harness 的**无损上下文归档 + 检索**插件。\n4: \n5: 当长对话导致本地模型 prefill 超时（provider 报告\n6: `pi-ai stream idle timeout`）或撑爆上下文窗口（`CONTEXT_WINDOW_EXCEEDED`）时，\n7: 本插件会：\n8: \n9: 1. 只保留最近的**消息**（至多 token 预算）在模型上下文里；\n10: 2. 把更早的消息**原样**归档到每个会话独立的持久化文件（不做摘要、不丢失）；\n11: 3. 用一条紧凑的\"已归档\"标记替换被移出的内容，并告诉模型如何取回；\n12: 4. 授权重试请求。\n13: \n14: 如果归档后仍不够（或表面已经很小），则回退到内置的 `dsh-compaction-basic`\n15: 做有损摘要兜底。模型通过 `context_sniper_recall` 工具检索归档内容。\n16: \n17: > **[English](README.md) | 中文**\n18: \n19: ## 为什么单独做一个插件\n20: \n21: `dsh-compaction-basic` 已经在做溢出恢复——但靠的是**摘要**（有损）。本插件是互补的：\n22: 靠**归档**（无损）恢复，并给模型一扇回到原文的门。它不改动任何 DSH 底层参数，\n23: 也不会关掉内置压缩。\n24: \n25: ## 你需要配置什么\n26: \n27: 三个参数面向用户，均可在**设置 → Context Sniper** 面板中编辑（持久化 + 热更新）：\n28: \n29: - **`surfaceTokenBudget`**——模型表面保留的最大 token 数，更早的消息全部归档。\n30:   这是**唯一的预算参数**，不存在独立的\"默认 Token 预算\"。\n31: - **`maxSearchHits`**——`context_sniper_recall` 每次查询返回的最大消息条数\n32:   （1–64，默认 8）。\n33: - **`hitMaxChars`**——每条归档消息在命中结果中包含的最大字符数\n34:   （200–20000，默认 4000）。\n35: \n36: 以上任意项（以及 `pressureRatio`、`archiveDir`、`verbose`）也可在 DSH 设置文档\n37: （命名空间 `dsh-context-sniper`）或组合配置（`config.*`）中设置。其余都有合理\n38: 默认值（见\"配置\"）。\n39: \n40: ## 如何工作\n41: \n42: 识别基于 **provider 的结构化 API 错误响应**。当 LLM API 返回超时或\n43: 上下文窗口溢出错误时，DSH 的 LLM adapter 设置 `failure.code`，agent 循环\n44: 通过 `agent/request-error` 瀑布将其暴露。\n45: \n46: 本插件以 `prepend: true` 注册该监听器，使其成为最外层包裹、最先行动：\n47: \n48: - 从最旧消息开始归档，直到表面 token ≤ 预算；\n49: - 返回终结动作 `{ kind: \"retry\" }`，请求随即针对收缩后的上下文重跑——\n50:   内置有损压缩因此不会执行。\n51: \n52: 若没有可安全归档的内容（表面已最小），则调用 `next()`，交给内置压缩兜底。\n53: \n54: 可选：设置 `pressureRatio`（如 `0.8`），在表面 token 超过预算该比例时**提前**\n55: 归档，避免硬失败。默认关闭（`0`）。\n56: \n57: ## 归档粒度\n58: \n59: 归档以**单条消息**为单位。表面是一组带 token 定价的节点（每条 user message、\n60: assistant message 或 tool result）。插件从最新节点向前累加 token，达到预算时\n61: 停止，更早的全部归档。工具调用配对安全检查确保切割不会把 tool-call 和\n62: 其 result 拆散。\n63: \n64: ## 标记合法性（为什么裁剪不再破坏会话）\n65: \n66: 裁剪时，本插件追加一条紧凑的 `user/message` 标记，携带\n67: `surfaceOp: { op: 'replace', start, end }`（与内置 `dsh-compaction` 同一机制），\n68: 在模型表面上\"影子化\"被归档的范围。原始事件仍保留在持久化日志中，\n69: 改变的只是模型可见的表面。\n70: \n71: **标记的 `data.id` 是必填项。** DSH 的会话加载边界（`@deepseek-ai/dsh-session`\n72: 的 `assertMessageEventShape`）会拒绝任何 `data.id` 不是非空字符串的 `user/message`，\n73: 抛出 `session event at seq N lacks an identified message`，并导致**整个会话无法加载**\n74: （`SessionPersistenceCorruptionError`）。早期插件版本省略了 `id`，这正是用户看到的\n75: 损坏。本版本始终生成非空 `id`（归档 UUID）并设置 `source.kind` 为 `plugin`，\n76: 因此每条标记都能无损地通过 DSH 持久化往返，裁剪后会话也能正常加载。\n77: \n78: ### 标记是指令，不只是提示\n79: \n80: 裁剪**不是**重开会话——模型应该继续它正在做的任务。但早期标记只是*通知*模型\n81: 内容被归档了，模型于是经常\"重启\"：重新读文件、重新自我介绍、重新规划——\n82: 消耗额外 token 和时间，甚至再次撑爆窗口。本版本把标记变成对模型的明确指令：\n83: \n84: - *\"这是一个上下文归档检查点——不是会话重启。你正在任务中途，请从你停下的地方\n85:   继续。\"*\n86: - *\"不要重新读文件、不要重新自我介绍、不要从头重新规划。\"*\n87: - *\"如果你缺少已不可见的事实、决策、文件内容或指令，调用\n88:   `context_sniper_recall(\"<关键词>\")` 检索归档原文。\"*\n89: - *\"先检索再依赖——不要凭猜测使用归档内容。\"*\n90: \n91: 由于标记同时通过 `surfaceOp: replace` 把被归档范围从模型表面移除，重试请求的\n92: **prompt 更短、prefill 更快**——这正是裁剪的意义。指令文本让模型保持在任务上，\n93: 不会通过重新探索来抵消这个加速。\n94: \n95: ## 归档存储位置（与 DSH 会话目录对齐）\n96: \n97: 每次归档一个 JSON 文件，存放在 **DSH 会话目录内**，使其与被裁剪的会话日志\n98: 同处一目录：\n99: \n100: ```\n101: <DSH_HOME>/sessions/<projectKey(cwd)>/<encodeSegment(sessionId)>/context-sniper/<archiveId>.json\n102: ```\n103: \n104: `<projectKey(cwd)>` 与 `<encodeSegment(sessionId)>` 使用 DSH\n105: `dsh-session-persistence-jsonl` 后端定位 `session.jsonl.zstd` 的**同一套算法**计算，\n106: 因此归档落在拥有该会话的同一目录中。`context-sniper/` 子目录对 DSH 的会话枚举\n107: 不可见（DSH 只把包含 `session.jsonl[.zstd]` 文件的目录当作会话），因此绝不会\n108: 干扰 DSH 的存储、列表或加载。\n109: \n110: ## 检索工具\n111: \n112: `context_sniper_recall(query)`——对当前会话的归档做关键词检索，按原文返回匹配的消息\n113: （最新在前），每条带角色、轮次与片段。模型在需要本会话早期、已不可见的事实、决策、\n114: 文件内容或指令时调用它。\n115: \n116: ## 配置\n117: \n118: | 键 | 默认 | 含义 |\n119: |---|---|---|\n120: | `surfaceTokenBudget` | `32768` | 模型表面保留的最大 token 数。 |\n121: | `pressureRatio` | `0` | 在预算该比例处提前归档；`0` = 仅在超时时反应。 |\n122: | `maxSearchHits` | `8` | 每次检索返回的最大归档消息数。 |\n123: | `hitMaxChars` | `4000` | 每条命中消息的最大字符数。 |\n124: | `archiveDir` | `context-sniper` | 每个 DSH 会话目录内的归档子目录。 |\n125: | `verbose` | `false` | 以 info 级别记录每次归档决策。 |\n126: \n127: ## 安装\n128: \n129: ``\n\n[... tool result middle pruned ...]\n\n每次重启所有设置都会恢复成默认值。**\n238: \n239: 根本原因：设置 schema 用 `z.number().int()` 构造，但 Schemastery 这个 schema\n240: 库**根本没有 `int()` 方法**（它提供的是 `number`、`natural`、`percent`，以及\n241: 实例方法 `min`/`max`/`step`/`default`）。所以 `z.object({...})` 在插件注册设置\n242: 命名空间的那一刻就抛出 `TypeError`；这个失败被 try/catch 吞掉，owner `scope`\n243: 一直是 `null`。`scope` 为 null 时，设置面板仍然会更新内存里的值（所以会话内\n244: 裁剪行为正常），但**从来没有把任何值写进 DSH 设置文档**——于是下次启动时\n245: 所有值都回退到组合配置的默认值。这也解释了为什么 `~/.dsh/settings.yaml` 里\n246: 压根没有 `dsh-context-sniper` 这一段。\n247: \n248: 修复：\n249: - 整数约束改用合法的 `step(1)` 形式（`z.number().step(1)…`）；同时\n250:   `surfaceTokenBudget` 不再强制 1024 的倍数（这样任意 ≥ 1024 的整数都能持久化）；\n251: - 保存 RPC 现在**先持久化、只有写入真正提交后才更新内存值**，并且把真实错误\n252:   回报给面板，而不是虚假的\"已保存\"；当值只在会话内生效、无法持久化（降级模式，\n253:   未挂载设置服务）时，面板会显示一条提示。\n254: \n255: ### v0.6.0\n256: \n257: - 无损归档 + 检索、超时/截断/溢出恢复、检索工具、设置面板。\n258: \n259: ## 局限\n260: \n261: - 关键词检索是确定性子串匹配，非语义检索——请用它实际会出现的词来查询。\n262: - 单条消息超过预算时无法拆分；如果整个表面就是一条超大消息，插件回退到内置压缩。\n263: - Token 估算来自 DSH token meter 的启发式（字符定价），非真实 tokenizer。\n\n(End of file - total 263 lines)\n</content>"
